cells.tense: The practice is holding right now, and it is holding you with it.
cells.ask: After one session this week, say one true sentence about what changed to one person. No explanation owed.
cells.core:
You have a practice going, and it is not eating you. Same small thing, done again, without a whip over it. That is the hard part and you are past it.

The real thing is what it does to the people around you. You come out of it easier to be near: steadier, more willing to listen, less in a hurry to be somewhere else. Quiet hours you would once have guarded like property now feed the room instead. Nothing here needs fixing. Keep it plain and keep it yours, and let the ones close to you see the difference rather than hear about it. What sits next to this sits around it, not on it, and the asking above is the whole size of it.
cells.sheetLine: Shown up without forcing it, and people feel it.
cells.verb: showing up to the same small thing again
cells.place: where another person is actually met

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you there is a version where it finally counts, and you are already there.
cells.ask: Stop one session five minutes early, on purpose, while it is still alive. Put the stop in your phone and obey the phone.
cells.core:
You are grinding. Same small thing, except the smallness has stopped being the point. Nothing you make is finished on the inside, so it goes back to the start, then back again, and the hours swell. You close off in a way that feels necessary, though from outside it looks like a choice.

This is the opposite of giving up. You are holding on so hard the practice has no room to breathe, and people get the shut door instead of you. That is what keeping it at this pitch costs.

The ask is a rehearsal for leaving while the thing still has life in it. Hands off the work. Do it once, not as quitting, and see that your grip is not what carries it.

cells.tense: Starting the practice again has gone badly before, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Pick one fifteen-minute block and put it on the same hook each day this week. Do it at half strength and count the showing up.
cells.core:
The practice keeps not lasting. You have started it more times than you can count and it does not take, and you have a good case for it. Whatever sits behind that, the flinch is real, and keeping a small thing lit keeps feeling like it asks more than it should.

What goes missing when it stops is not the skill. It is what a steady hour does to your patience with people. Without the small light, close contact burns hotter, and you pull the chair back.

So the ask is below what you could do, deliberately. Not a performance and not a build. Keep it small enough that it cannot scare you, until being at it once more stops being a door and starts being a chair.

cells.tense: The practicing is already running, and you would tell anyone it is not.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing people already count on you for, and set it where they can reach it on purpose this week.
cells.core:
You are further along than you let yourself say. It shows as speed in company you call being yourself, and in a calm that others accept as ordinary while you call it nothing. You have put in the hours that make it look natural.

The face of the practice is flow without force and hours that connect rather than shut people out. It lives that way with the humans around you.

Set the one thing where they can reach it, once, without explaining. More than one thing and you have built a curriculum, so choose the one you would already deny. You can still call it not-a-practice, if that makes the hands steadier. What you set down does not need the title.
cells.sheetLine: Already steady, and still calling it nothing.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say what past made practice feel dangerous for this person, so Too Little must stay at the level of the flinch and never name an event, a person, or a duration. A reader could reasonably say they have no trouble keeping a practice, only with people, so each cell leans on the first thing the other can see and leaves the judgement theirs to make. The ask still clears a usable step if the read is wrong: showing up, releasing the gripping, offering steadiness, or putting a chosen stop on a clock all work without buying the diagnosis. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about the morning or the day 'coming out different'; struck from all four.
